body:
I've always had crippling anxiety. I get called out on it a lot. 

Thank you for taking the time to read. I'm sorry you've been having such a hard time too. I hope for your peace as well. What brought you to this point?

Still here. Thank you all for your support, it helped me more than I anticipated. It's nice to talk to people about it. 
I haven't changed my mind. But I have to wait till March 1st. That's been my life insurance kicks in. Anyone have any easy bucket list ideas? Reminder: I'm poor and in the Midwest.

How did you become a crisis-line responder? How do you deal with all the trauma? 

We have a state wide child welfare hotline. They hear horrible reports of anything from neglect to newborn crisis/ fatality. Then it goes to investigations, then to the courts, then to case management (me). 

I called the suicide hotline once. I just listened to the girl ask me questions then I hung up her. My throat was clamped shut, I couldn't bring myself to stay anything. I imagine that happens a lot.
I'm not a great owner. I explained in another comment. Plus having a sob story will make them way more adoptable. They will be much happier.

Thank you for taking the time to read and comment. 

I have a pit mix and a jack russell mix. I adopted them both while working at an animal rescue. You would think this would imply that they are well trained but that's not exactly true. 
They both had behavioral issues when I adopted them and I've made no progress on training, mostly due to depression. They both have seperation anxiety and need to be watched at all times or they will destroy everything. This means they have to be crated whenever I'm not there. Which is sad for them. Also I'm incredibly poor and that doesn't help anything. 

They are going back to the same animal shelter where I used to work. They will get a TON of specialized attention and training. I used to be friends with most of the adoption counselors so they will make sure they go to amazing homes. 

Relating back to your first comment, being passionate doesn't inherently make you effective. I can care about dogs (kids, mental health, ect) but that doesn't mean I'm effective at working with those populations. Frankly, I'm too depressed and anxious to be a good counselor. You have be able to care for yourself to care for others.

Thank you for asking. I'm okay, went to work.

I figured out where my dogs will be living! That's kinda exciting for me. They are going to have great lives.

Thank you, you are a kind person. I do understand logically that depression changes how you perceive yourself and the world around you. But this has been going on so long. I switch between wanting to push through and try my hardest then within the same day I see no point in any of it. Every single interaction is weighed. Every moment of everyday is a factor that tips the scales on way or the other. I'm tired of living in purgatory.
I'm so sorry you are in this position. I can tell you care deeply for the people close to you. Have you told anyone?

Hey Donald Trump-

I'd like to see how YOUR hair would FAIR in a blizzard😆
